entities.name: Li Zhengji
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Li Zhengji (Yi Jeonggi; né Li Huaiyu, d. 781) was a Tang general and regional strongman of Goguryeo descent who dominated Pinglu and related northeastern circuits after the An Lushan Rebellion. Rising through military service on the northeastern frontier, he converted wartime command into hereditary provincial power typical of late Tang jiedushi politics.

His career shows how non-Han military lineages and frontier armies became indispensable once the court lost direct control of Hebei and the northeast. Successive Tang emperors bargained with him for grain, cavalry, and nominal loyalty while conceding fiscal and appointment rights on the ground.

Li Zhengji’s polity helped set the pattern of semi-autonomous northeastern commands that constrained Tang recovery and shaped the balance between court and provinces into the ninth century.
